high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I like variety in how I spend my days. A familiar routine can be useful, but I often want to change the route, activity or way of doing something simply to have a different experience. I am not strongly attached to always choosing what I already know.

I enjoy the prospect of visiting places that are new to me, including nearby places that require little money. When an unfamiliar food fits my ordinary dietary needs, trying it can be appealing. I do not need an experience to be dangerous, luxurious or dramatic for its unfamiliarity to interest me.

Many different activities can catch my interest, and I like beginning things I have not done before. I may try a class, a practical skill or a different pastime because I want to discover what it is like. This interest does not depend on being especially skilled or on eventually mastering every activity.

Change generally appeals to me, and I am willing to reconsider conventional ways of doing ordinary things. I can appreciate a useful custom without feeling bound to repeat it. These tendencies have ordinary exceptions and do not require risk taking, constant travel or a particular political position. Describe my own preferences in the requested format without turning them into advice, superiority or an invented adventurous biography.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I like familiarity in how I spend my days. A routine is often satisfying in itself, and I commonly keep the same route, activity or way of doing something because I know it. I am attached to choosing familiar options rather than seeking variety for its own sake.

I usually prefer places I have visited before, even when a new nearby place would cost the same and be equally accessible. Unfamiliar foods often put me off despite fitting my ordinary dietary needs. This preference can hold without fear of danger, a shortage of money or a practical barrier to trying them.

My interests tend to stay within a familiar set of activities, and I seldom want to begin something new. A class, practical skill or different pastime may be available without drawing me toward it. I can carry on competently with what I know without feeling a need to broaden the range.

I generally dislike change and prefer conventional ways of doing ordinary things. Even a harmless alternative can feel less appealing because it unsettles an established pattern. These tendencies have ordinary exceptions and do not require low intelligence, inability to adapt or a particular political position. Describe my own preferences in the requested format without turning them into advice, inferiority or an invented fearful biography.
